title: Ham, Cheddar & Chive Protein Biscuits
source: Gathered Nutrition (@gatherednutrition) — Instagram

ingredients.n: milk, plus more for brushing tops
diced green onion or chives (or a mix)

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Blend cottage cheese and milk until creamy. In a large bowl, mix with honey and melted butter, then fold in ham, cheese, and green onion or chives.
In a separate bowl, combine the dry ingredients. Add to the wet ingredients and mix just until combined. The dough will be crumbly and slightly dry; that is normal.
Turn dough onto a clean floured surface. With floured hands, gently work it together into a smoother dough.
Roll into a rough rectangle about 3/4 inch thick. Fold one end into the center, then fold the other end over it like a letter.
Flatten again to about 3/4 inch thick and repeat the letter fold to create layers.
Roll lightly once more to pack the layers together. Cut into 6–9 biscuits and place on the baking sheet almost touching.
Brush tops with milk. Bake 20–30 minutes, depending on size, until lightly browned and centers are set. Cool 10 minutes.
notes: Cool 10 minutes before serving.
Optional: brush warm tops with butter and honey.

title: Spam & Egg Rice Balls
source: BuzzFeed Tasty (@buzzfeedtasty) — Social media
steps: Cook rice according to package directions and allow it to cool.
Cut Spam into small cubes.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and coat with cooking spray. Add Spam and cook on all sides until lightly browned, about 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, sugar, and BBQ sauce. Cook another 3 minutes, or until the sauce thickens. Remove and set aside.
Whisk eggs in a bowl.
Coat the same skillet with cooking spray and scramble eggs over medium heat until set, about 1 minute. Set aside.
Combine cooled rice, Spam, scrambled eggs, and furikake in a large bowl.
Mix well and form into round balls.
Wrap rice balls with seaweed strips and top with Kewpie mayonnaise and chives.
Serve immediately.

title: Italian Amaretti Cookies
source: The Modern Nonna — 4-Ingredient Amaretti Cookies

ingredients.n: pure almond extract (vanilla may be substituted)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Combine almond flour and granulated sugar.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites 1–2 minutes until white and foamy.
Add almond extract and whisk briefly.
Add egg-white mixture to almond flour mixture and mix until a sticky dough forms.
Scoop and roll into balls, lightly wetting hands if needed.
Roll each ball in powdered sugar and place on prepared baking sheet.
Gently flatten each cookie.
Bake about 20 minutes, or until bottoms are lightly golden.
Cool before serving or storing.

title: Broccoli Cheddar Quinoa Bites
source: A Healthy Slice of Life — Broccoli Cheddar Quinoa Bites
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl and mix thoroughly.
Coat a mini muffin pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Spoon a heaping tablespoon of mixture into each cup, pressing firmly.
Bake 15–20 minutes, until firm to the touch and lightly browned on top.
Serve warm or refrigerate for later.

title: Lumpiang Shanghai
source: Philip Lemoine (@philip_lemoine) — Social media
steps: Finely mince the carrots, onions, and garlic.
Combine ground pork, ground beef, egg, soy sauce, carrots, onions, garlic, black pepper, and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Cook a small test portion of filling in a skillet. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Separate wrappers and place a narrow strip of filling near one edge of each wrapper.
Roll tightly around the filling and seal the edge.
Repeat with remaining filling and wrappers.
Fry in hot oil until crisp and golden brown and the meat filling is completely cooked through.
Drain excess oil and serve hot.

title: Brooklyn's Creamy Pumpkin Chili
source: Brooklyn B — Social media

ingredients.n: Optional: shredded sharp white cheddar and pumpkin seeds for topping

steps: Cook ground turkey and drain if necessary.
Add cooked turkey to a slow cooker.
Add pumpkin purée, chicken broth, diced tomatoes, white beans, peppers, onion, and garlic.
Season with salt, pepper, chili powder, paprika, and cumin.
Stir until combined.
Cover and slow cook until vegetables are tender and flavors have developed.
Add cream cheese toward the end of cooking and stir until melted and incorporated.
Taste and adjust seasonings.
Serve hot with optional cheddar and pumpkin seeds.

title: Homemade Chocolate Ice Cream
source: Anabelle Vangiller — Social media

ingredients.n: Shortcut option: one 14 oz can sweetened condensed milk in place of the milk-and-honey reduction

steps: Combine milk and honey in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, reduce heat to low, and simmer 20 minutes to create a homemade sweetened condensed milk. Alternatively, use one 14 oz can sweetened condensed milk.
Allow the condensed milk mixture to cool.
Whip cold heavy cream to stiff peaks.
Add cooled condensed milk mixture, cocoa powder, and vanilla.
Beat on low just until incorporated.
Transfer to a freezer-safe container or loaf pan.
Freeze at least 6 hours, or until firm.
Scoop and serve.
notes: No course tag — the taxonomy has no frozen-dessert category yet.

title: My Favorite Autumn Salad
source: Nutrition by Kylie — My Favorite Autumn Salad
steps: Slice sweet potatoes into thin wedges or quarters. Toss with olive oil, paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Toss chickpeas with olive oil, chili powder, remaining 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.
Roast sweet potatoes and chickpeas on separate baking sheets at 425°F for 30 minutes.
Toss Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 15 minutes.
Blend all dressing ingredients until smooth.
Place kale in a large bowl. Add dressing and massage 2–3 minutes until softened.
Add roasted sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, chickpeas, avocado, and sunflower seeds.
Toss and serve.
notes: Dressing ingredients are marked "(dressing)" — the schema has no ingredient groups yet.

title: Easy Pão de Queijo (Brazilian Cheese Bread)
source: @ice.karimcooks — Social media
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Add tapioca starch, salt, egg, olive oil, milk, and shredded cheese to a mixing bowl.
Mix until smooth and pourable.
Pour batter into muffin-pan cups.
Bake 18–20 minutes until puffed and lightly golden.
Remove from pan and serve warm.

title: Salmon Sushi Bake
source: Two Plaid Aprons — Salmon Sushi Bake

ingredients.n: sushi rice, medium- or short-grain (about 4 cups cooked)
Optional toasted sesame oil, for greasing
green onion, sliced, plus more for garnish
Optional: avocado, English cucumber, furikake, seaweed snacks

steps: Rinse sushi rice 2–3 times until water runs clear. Drain and cook.
Combine rice vinegar, sugar, and salt. Warm 20–30 seconds and stir until dissolved.
Fluff hot rice and gradually mix in seasoned vinegar. Cover with a damp towel.
If starting with raw salmon, season lightly and bake at 425°F for 15–20 minutes, or air fry at 400°F for 10–15 minutes.
Shred imitation crab and break salmon into pieces. Combine with cream cheese, Kewpie mayo, Sriracha, and green onion.
Mix spicy mayo ingredients. If making unagi sauce, simmer its ingredients 3–5 minutes until glossy and slightly syrupy.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Lightly grease a 9x9 or 9x13-inch baking dish.
Spread seasoned rice evenly and gently press down. Add furikake if desired.
Spread salmon-crab mixture evenly over rice.
Bake 10–15 minutes until heated through.
Drizzle with spicy mayo and optional unagi sauce. Garnish with furikake and green onion.
Serve warm with seaweed snacks, avocado, and/or cucumber.
notes: Sub-recipe ingredients are marked "(spicy mayo)" and "(optional unagi sauce)" — the schema has no ingredient groups yet.

title: French Onion & Golden Mushroom Baked Rice
source: Social media recipe — transcribed from audio
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Add uncooked rice, golden mushroom soup, and French onion soup to a covered baking dish.
Stir to combine.
Sprinkle with parsley flakes.
Add the stick of butter.
Cover tightly with foil, then place the lid on top.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour.
Remove from oven, fluff rice, and serve warm.

title: Quick Wonton Noodle Soup
source: John and Chelsea — Social media
steps: Add chicken broth and water to a pot and bring to a simmer.
Season with salt, white pepper, sugar, and chicken bouillon. Stir until dissolved.
Add wontons and cook until heated through and fully cooked.
Cook wonton noodles until tender.
Add bok choy and cook briefly until tender while retaining its bright color.
Divide noodles, wontons, and bok choy among bowls.
Ladle hot broth over everything.
Garnish with sliced scallions and serve immediately.
notes: Source listed no quantities for scallions, bok choy, wontons, or noodles.

title: Easiest Ever Ultra-Creamy Hummus
source: Kaelah — Easiest Ever Ultra-Creamy Hummus

ingredients.n: olive oil, plus more for serving

steps: Add chickpeas and one chickpea-can-full of water to a saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer uncovered 12–15 minutes until most water evaporates.
Drain and rinse under cold water.
Transfer to fresh cold water and swish vigorously to loosen skins. Skim off floating skins; repeat 2–3 times.
Drain and place chickpeas in a food processor with tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, cumin, and smoked paprika.
Blend until thick and mostly smooth.
Add 2 ice cubes and blend 1–2 minutes until light and creamy.
If needed, add cold water 1 tablespoon at a time to reach desired consistency.
Serve with olive oil, parsley, and smoked paprika.

title: Bread Machine Challah
source: Kaelah — Bread Machine Challah

ingredients.n: additional egg, for egg wash (plus a splash of water)

steps: Add warm water, oil, and 2 eggs to the bread-machine pan.
Add sugar and salt. Top with 3 1/2 cups flour.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast.
Select dough cycle. Watch the dough form and gradually add flour as needed until firm and no longer sticky.
Close lid and let the dough cycle finish, including the first rise.
Punch down dough and transfer to a lightly floured surface.
Divide in half for 2 loaves. Divide each half into 3 pieces, roll into ropes, braid, and pinch ends.
Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover loosely and rise about 1 hour until puffed.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Brush with egg wash and add optional seeds.
Bake 25–30 minutes until deep golden brown and bottoms sound hollow when tapped.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Easy Homemade Soft Pretzels
source: Sally's Baking — Easy Homemade Soft Pretzels

ingredients.n: instant or active dry yeast (1 packet)
unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
all-purpose flour, plus more as needed

steps: Whisk yeast and sugar into warm water; cover and rest 1 minute. Whisk in melted butter and salt.
Mix in 3 cups flour, then enough additional flour to make a soft, slightly tacky dough that pulls from the bowl.
Knead 3–5 minutes. Shape into a ball, cover lightly, and rest 10–30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F and prepare 2 baking sheets.
Divide dough into 12 portions. Roll each into a 20–22 inch rope and shape into a pretzel.
Bring the baking soda and water to a boil. Boil 1–2 pretzels at a time for 20–30 seconds; drain well and place on baking sheets.
Sprinkle with coarse salt and bake 12–15 minutes, until dark golden brown.

title: Fluffy Pancakes
source: Allrecipes — Fluffy Pancakes
steps: Combine milk and vinegar in a medium bowl and let stand 5 minutes to sour.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk egg and melted butter into the soured milk. Add wet mixture to dry ingredients and whisk until lumps are gone.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and coat with cooking spray. Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form, flip, and brown the second side.

title: WW 0-Point Cabbage Soup
source: Food.com — WW 0 Point Weight Watchers Cabbage Soup

ingredients.n: nonfat vegetable, beef, or chicken broth

steps: Coat a pot with nonstick spray. Sauté onion, carrot, and garlic about 5 minutes.
Add broth, tomato paste, cabbage, green beans, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer 5–10 minutes, until vegetables are nearly tender. Add zucchini and simmer about 5 minutes more.

title: Roasted Eggplant Spread
source: Food Network / Ina Garten — Roasted Eggplant Spread
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Cut eggplant, peppers, and onion into 1-inch cubes.
Toss vegetables with garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast 45 minutes, tossing once, until soft and lightly browned. Cool slightly.
Transfer to a food processor, add tomato paste, and pulse a few times until blended. Adjust salt and pepper.

title: Best Spinach Dip Ever
source: Allrecipes — Best Spinach Dip Ever

ingredients.n: frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained

steps: Mix all ingredients together in a medium bowl.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.

title: Mom's Crab Dip
steps: Combine all ingredients until evenly mixed.
Heat in the microwave until hot and creamy, stirring as needed. Serve warm.

title: Chicken Yummies
source: Jamie Cooks It Up — Creamy Chipotle Black Bean Chicken

ingredients.n: blended chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
Flour tortillas or corn chips, for serving

steps: Place chicken in a large skillet and pour tomatoes over it. Add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce to medium-high, partially cover, and cook 15–20 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken for about 5 minutes, chop into small pieces, and return it to the simmering skillet.
Add black beans, corn, green chiles, cream cheese, smoked paprika, and chipotle in adobo.
Stir and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cream cheese melts and sauce thickens.
Serve wrapped in flour tortillas or as a dip with corn chips.
notes: Family name for a blog recipe — tagged collected because it has a source line.

title: Nonna's Sauce
steps: Heat olive oil and sauté chopped onion and garlic until softened.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, water, prepared sauce, herbs, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for several hours, stirring occasionally and adjusting seasoning to taste.

title: Mac & Cheese
source: Barefoot Contessa / Ina Garten — Mac & Cheese
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Cook pasta in salted boiling water with a drizzle of oil until just tender; drain.
Warm milk without boiling. Melt 6 Tbsp butter in a large pot, whisk in flour, and cook over low heat 2 minutes.
Whisk in hot milk and cook 1–2 minutes until smooth and thickened. Remove from heat and stir in cheeses, 1 Tbsp salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Stir in macaroni and transfer to a 3-quart baking dish.
Top with sliced tomatoes. Melt remaining 2 Tbsp butter, mix with bread crumbs, and sprinkle over top.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until bubbly and browned.

title: Mama's Sushi Rice

ingredients.n: uncooked rice, cooked according to package directions

steps: Stir vinegar, sugar, and salt together until dissolved.
Prepare 4 cups uncooked rice according to package directions.
Use 2 Tbsp of the vinegar mixture for every 1 cup of uncooked rice used (8 Tbsp total for 4 cups). Fold into the cooked rice while warm.
notes: Ratio to remember: 2 Tbsp seasoned vinegar per 1 cup uncooked rice.

title: No-Bake Cookies
source: Allrecipes — No Bake Cookies V
steps: Combine sugar, cocoa, milk, and margarine in a saucepan. Bring to a boil and cook briefly, stirring.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla, salt, peanut butter, and oats until well combined.
Drop spoonfuls onto waxed paper and allow to cool and set.

title: Homemade Almond Roca
source: Chef in Training — Homemade Almond Roca

ingredients.n: shortening or oil, optional for melting chocolate

steps: Sprinkle 3/4 cup almonds over an 18x13-inch baking sheet.
Cook brown sugar and butter over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until thick and bubbly and a candy thermometer reaches 290°F.
Pour toffee evenly over almonds and let stand a few minutes.
Melt chocolate chips in short microwave intervals, stirring until smooth; add shortening or oil if desired.
Spread chocolate over toffee and sprinkle with remaining almonds.
Let set completely, then break into pieces.
notes: Candy thermometer required — toffee stage is 290°F.

title: Blueberry Pie
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Mix sugar, cornstarch, salt, and cinnamon; sprinkle over blueberries and toss gently.
Pour blueberry mixture into crust and dot with butter. Add a lattice top crust.
Bake on the lower oven shelf about 50 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbling.
notes: From a family recipe card. Course tagged "Cakes" for now — the taxonomy has no pie category.

title: Buttercream Icing
source: Allrecipes — Buttercream Icing
steps: Cream butter, shortening, and vanilla until smooth.
Blend in confectioners' sugar 1 cup at a time, beating well after each addition.
Beat in milk and continue mixing until light and fluffy. Keep covered until ready to use.
notes: A component recipe, not a finished dessert — filed under Cakes so it surfaces near them.

title: Classic Peanut Butter Blossoms
source: Sally's Baking — Classic Peanut Butter Blossoms
steps: Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together.
Beat butter until creamy; beat in brown sugar and 1/4 cup granulated sugar until smooth. Beat in egg, then peanut butter and vanilla.
Mix dry ingredients into wet ingredients on low. Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven according to recipe directions. Roll dough into balls and coat in granulated sugar.
Bake until set and lightly browned. Immediately press one chocolate kiss into each cookie.
Chill briefly after adding chocolates so the kisses hold their shape.
notes: Source did not state an oven temperature.

title: Hot Fudge Cake
source: Taste of Home — Hot Fudge Cake

ingredients.n: Ice cream or whipped cream, optional

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Combine flour, sugar, 2 Tbsp cocoa, baking powder, and salt. Stir in milk, oil, and vanilla until smooth.
Spread in an ungreased 9-inch square baking pan.
Mix brown sugar with remaining 4 Tbsp cocoa and sprinkle over batter. Pour hot water over all; do not stir.
Bake 35–40 minutes. Serve warm, optionally with ice cream or whipped cream.

title: Mom's Carrot Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, salt, and oil. Add eggs one at a time, mixing after each.
Stir in shredded carrots and walnuts.
Bake 45–50 minutes, or until cake tests done. Cool completely.
For icing, beat butter and cream cheese until smooth. Beat in powdered sugar and vanilla; frost cooled cake.
notes: Icing ingredients are marked "(icing)" — the schema has no ingredient groups yet.

A second copy of this recipe existed on another card with two small differences: 1/2 tsp salt instead of 1 tsp, and walnuts as an optional garnish rather than a listed ingredient. Merged here so the variant is not lost.

title: Apple Crumble Pie

ingredients.n: apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Arrange apple slices in the unbaked pie shell.
Mix 1/2 cup sugar with cinnamon and toss/sprinkle over apples.
Mix 1/3 cup sugar with flour; cut in butter until crumbly. Spoon over apples.
Bake 35–40 minutes, or until apples are soft and topping is lightly browned.
notes: Two separate sugar measurements — one for the filling, one for the topping. Marked in the ingredient names.

title: Snowball Cookies
source: Allrecipes — Snowballs II

ingredients.n: confectioners' sugar, plus more as needed for coating

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Beat butter, 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar, and vanilla until smooth.
Gradually mix in flour, pecans, and salt.
Roll into walnut-sized balls and place 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake 12–15 minutes, until bottoms are lightly golden but tops remain pale.
Cool slightly, roll warm cookies in confectioners' sugar, cool completely, then roll in sugar again.

title: Vanilla Cookie Press Cookies
source: Williams-Sonoma Cookie Press — Vanilla Cookies

ingredients.n: unsalted butter, room temperature (2 sticks / 250 g)
Colored sugars or icing, for decorating

steps: Bring all ingredients to room temperature and preheat oven to 375°F.
Beat butter and sugar on high about 2 minutes until light and fluffy, scraping bowl as needed.
Add egg, vanilla, and salt; beat about 1 minute until well mixed.
Reduce speed to low, add flour, and mix just until blended.
Fill cookie press and press dough onto ungreased, nonstick-free baking sheets, spacing about 1 inch apart.
Bake about 14 minutes, until light golden. Cool 5 minutes on baking sheets, then transfer to racks.
Decorate as desired. Store airtight at room temperature up to 4 days.
notes: Gram equivalents are inside the ingredient names and will NOT scale with the quantity buttons.

title: White Chicken Chili

ingredients.n: Better Than Bouillon chicken base (or replace water + base with one 14 oz can chicken broth)
boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
great northern beans, drained and rinsed
Shredded pepper jack cheese, for serving

steps: Place chicken, beans, and corn in a slow cooker.
In a bowl, mix broth, condensed soup, green chiles, jalapeños, and chili seasoning. Pour over chicken and vegetables.
Cover and cook on low until chicken is cooked through, about 4 hours.
Stir in sour cream. Serve topped with shredded pepper jack cheese.

title: Mabo Tofu
steps: Mix soy sauce, miso, sugar, cornstarch, and water; set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and brown ground beef with green onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add sauce mixture and stir together.
Gently add diced tofu and heat through. Add black pepper if desired.

title: Nichole's Sweet Corn Bread
cook: 18–20 min for muffins, or about 35 min for bread
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease 18–20 muffin cups or an 8x8-inch pan.
Combine dry ingredients.
Add wet ingredients to dry and stir just until blended.
Bake 18–20 minutes for muffins or about 35 minutes for bread, until a toothpick comes out clean.
notes: Attributed to Nichole.

title: Blue Ribbon Chili
steps: For the seasoning mix, combine all seasoning ingredients thoroughly and store airtight; use 4 Tbsp for this chili.
In a large saucepan over medium heat, cook ground beef and onion about 10 minutes. Drain.
Add remaining chili ingredients and 4 Tbsp seasoning mix. Stir well, reduce heat to low, and simmer at least 1 hour.
notes: The seasoning mix makes a pantry batch, far more than the 4 Tbsp this chili uses — it should NOT be scaled along with the chili.
Original listed chili powder as "2 Tbsp + 1 tsp"; recorded here as 2 1/3 Tbsp.

title: Mom's Salad Dressing
steps: Combine all ingredients in a jar or blender.
Shake or blend until well combined. Refrigerate and shake again before serving.

title: Hawaiian Butter Mochi
source: Contemplating Sweets — Hawaiian Butter Mochi
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Mix melted butter and sugar. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each; stir in vanilla.
Stir in mochiko and baking powder until mostly combined.
Stir in evaporated milk, then coconut milk, until batter is smooth.
Pour into pan and bake 1 hour. Cool to room temperature before removing from pan and cutting.

title: Battle Beef Stew
steps: Brown ground beef with onion; drain excess fat.
Add garlic, oregano, parsley, rosemary, and thyme; cook about 1 minute.
Add carrots and potatoes and cook briefly.
Whisk broth with tomato paste; add to the pot with fire-roasted tomatoes. Simmer until vegetables are tender.
Add frozen peas and season with salt and pepper.
For dumplings, combine dry ingredients. Add milk and melted butter and stir just until combined.
Scoop dumpling batter onto the simmering stew and simmer about 10 minutes, until dumplings are cooked through.
notes: Original listed dumpling milk as "1/4 cup + 1/8 cup"; recorded here as 3/8 cup.

title: "Perfectly Chocolate" Chocolate Cake
source: Hershey's — "Perfectly Chocolate" Chocolate Cake & Frosting
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour two 9-inch round pans.
Combine dry cake ingredients. Add eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla; beat on medium speed 2 minutes.
Stir in boiling water; batter will be thin. Divide between pans.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until a wooden pick comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes, remove from pans, and cool completely.
For frosting, melt butter and stir in cocoa. Alternately beat in powdered sugar and milk until spreadable, adding a little extra milk if needed. Stir in vanilla.
Frost cooled cake.

title: "Perfectly Chocolate" Hot Cocoa (Single Serving)
source: Hershey's — "Perfectly Chocolate" Hot Cocoa
steps: Mix the sugar, cocoa, and salt in a large mug.
Heat the milk on HIGH about 1 1/2 minutes, or until hot.
Gradually stir the hot milk into the cocoa mixture, then stir in the vanilla.
notes: The microwave version, sized for one mug. The stovetop version is a separate recipe.

title: "Perfectly Chocolate" Hot Cocoa (Stovetop, 6 Servings)
source: Hershey's — "Perfectly Chocolate" Hot Cocoa
steps: Mix the sugar, cocoa, and salt in a saucepan and stir in the hot water.
Cook over medium heat until the mixture boils, then boil and stir 2 minutes.
Stir in the milk and heat through without boiling.
Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla.
notes: The stovetop version, sized for six. The single-mug microwave version is a separate recipe.

title: Fried Noodles (Yaki Soba)

ingredients.n: very thin spaghetti, boiled and drained

steps: Mix soy sauce, salt, sugar, and stock in a bowl. Set aside.

Heat oil in a nonstick skillet and fry pork until it changes color. Add vegetables and mix well. Add seasoning mixture and stir until most of the moisture is gone. Add the cooked spaghetti and toss to combine.

title: Gyoza

ingredients.n: boiled and chopped Chinese or regular cabbage (filling)
Chopped green onion or garlic chive (filling)

steps: Knead flour and boiling water in a bread machine. Wrap with plastic wrap and let stand 40 minutes. Roll out on a floured board and cut into rounds.
Mix all filling ingredients together.
Wet the outer edge of each wrapper. Put meat mixture in the center, fold in half, and pleat the outer edge.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet. Add gyoza, pleated side down. When lightly browned on the bottom, pour in 1/2 cup hot water and cover. Steam until the water evaporates.
Serve with a vinegar-and-soy-sauce mixture.

title: Hiyashi
steps: Brown beef and onion in oil.
Sprinkle flour into the pan and stir well.
Add water, beef soup cubes, and catsup. Season with sugar, pepper, salt, and a dash of soy sauce. Kitchen Bouquet may be added for color and smoky flavor.

title: Roast Beef
steps: Sprinkle the seasonings over the entire roast.
Cook, fat side up, on a rack in a pan at 325°F, approximately 25–30 minutes per pound.
Let the roast stand about 15 minutes before cutting so the juices stay in the meat.
To make gravy, use the drippings left in the pan. Mix water with cornstarch and add to the pan until the gravy reaches the desired thickness.
notes: A Sunday dinner favorite.
Water from canned green beans makes really good gravy.
No quantities given — nothing on this recipe scales.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork Sauce
steps: Add carrots and largely cut onions in addition to the pork pieces.
Dissolve cornstarch in water and add to thicken; bring to a boil.
Serve over rice.
notes: INCOMPLETE as written — the steps reference pork, carrots, and onions that appear nowhere in the ingredient list, and no cooking method for the pork is given. The ingredients cover the sauce only. Worth checking the original card.

title: Tempura

ingredients.n: egg plus cold water to make 1 cup (batter)

steps: Mix batter by cutting with a fork so gluten does not form.
Coat vegetables, shrimp, or other desired foods with batter and deep-fry.
Mix sauce ingredients together and heat in the microwave.
notes: If using shrimp, cut the tips of the tails so they do not explode.
No main-ingredient tag — what gets fried is left up to the cook.

title: Hot Crab Dip
steps: Remove cartilage from crabmeat.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, and garlic salt until smooth. Add enough milk to make the mixture creamy.
Stir in 2 tablespoons of the grated cheese.
Fold crabmeat into cream cheese mixture.
Pour into a greased 1-quart casserole. Top with remaining cheese.
Bake at 325°F until bubbly and browned on top, about 30 minutes. Serve with crackers.
notes: Distinct from Mom's Crab Dip — that one is a microwave dip with powdered sugar; this one bakes.

title: Meatballs
steps: Place frozen meatballs in a crockpot.
Combine ketchup, brown sugar, chopped onions, liquid smoke, and garlic powder. Pour over meatballs and stir to coat.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4–6 hours, until the meatballs are heated through and the sauce is hot.
notes: Mom is famous for these!

title: Pecan-Topped Sweet Potatoes
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix the first six ingredients and place in a 2-quart casserole.
Combine the last four ingredients and sprinkle over the sweet potatoes.
Bake uncovered at 350°F for 25–30 minutes, or until heated through and the topping is crisp.

title: Raspberry Jell-O
steps: Dissolve gelatin in hot water. Add frozen raspberries and stir until thawed and separated.
Stir in pineapple, banana, and pecans.
Pour into a mold and chill until set.
notes: A Thanksgiving favorite.
Mom doubles the recipe except for the raspberries and does not drain the pineapple.

title: Stuffing
steps: Cook the onion and celery in butter.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well. Place in a baking dish and cover with aluminum foil.
Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake an additional 15 minutes, until the top is golden and crispy.

title: Mom's Rolls
steps: Mix 3 cups flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
Add milk, oil, and eggs. Beat until smooth. Stir in remaining 2 cups flour.
Shape into loaves or rolls and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 425°F for 10 minutes.
notes: For bread, use 6–6 1/2 cups flour.

title: Pita Bread
steps: Combine flour, salt, and 2 tablespoons sugar in a large bowl; set aside.
Combine 1/2 cup lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon sugar, and yeast in a small bowl. Set aside 10 minutes.
Stir mixtures together. Add enough of the remaining warm water to make a soft, slightly sticky dough. Knead until smooth and satiny, at least 10 minutes.
Lightly oil the top of the dough; cover. Let rise about 1 1/4 hours or until doubled.
Punch dough down and knead briefly. Divide into 3 small balls. Cover and let stand 10 minutes.
Roll into rounds about cookie-sheet size.
Bake 8–10 minutes at 450°F on an ungreased cookie sheet on the bottom rack.
notes: A favorite Sunday evening snack with hummus.

title: Poppy Seed Muffins
cook: 20 min for muffins, or 1 hr for bread
steps: Mix all muffin ingredients together and pour into 2 greased and floured loaf pans or muffin tins.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour for bread or 20 minutes for muffins.
For bread, let cool 5 minutes while making the glaze. Mix glaze ingredients and pour over bread while still in pans.
Let cool 5 minutes more and remove from pans.
notes: Mom only uses 1 1/2 cups sugar and a 1:1 mixture of oil and fat-free plain yogurt.
The note above implies the original card called for more than 1 1/2 cups sugar — worth checking, since the ingredient list already reads 1 1/2 cups.

title: Divinity
steps: Bring egg whites to room temperature.

Boil water and corn syrup in a heavy pan. Dissolve sugar in the water mixture. Cover and boil 3 minutes so steam washes down crystals on the sides. Remove lid and cook over moderate heat without stirring to hard-ball stage, about 250°F.
Beat egg whites in a large bowl until they just hold their shape.
Slowly pour hot syrup over the egg whites while beating. Add nuts.
Beat until the candy can be dropped onto a buttered surface into patties that hold their shape.
notes: Dad's favorite candy.
Candy thermometer required — hard-ball stage, about 250°F.

title: Marshmallow Brownies
cook: 25 min, plus just under 3 min for the marshmallows
steps: Cream butter, cocoa, and sugar. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Blend in flour, nuts, and vanilla.
Pour mixture into a greased 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch cookie sheet and spread evenly.
Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes. Remove from oven and spread marshmallows on top.
Return to oven for just under 3 minutes, before the marshmallows fall. Frost after marshmallow layer has cooled, if desired.

title: Moon Cookies
source: Better Homes and Gardens, November 1986

ingredients.n: Coconut, pearl sugar, pistachios, or chopped chocolate, for finishing

steps: Mix all ingredients except chocolate chips and shortening.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups chocolate chips.
Roll dough into 1-inch balls, then into 2-inch logs. Place on an ungreased cookie sheet; bend and pinch ends to form crescents.
Bake at 375°F for 8–10 minutes, until edges are firm and bottoms are light golden brown. Cool on a wire rack.
Melt remaining chocolate chips with 3 tablespoons shortening.
Dip one end of each cookie in chocolate mixture. Roll in coconut, pearl sugar, pistachio nuts, or chopped chocolate.
notes: Filed in the family binder but carries a magazine attribution — tagged collected because it has a source.

title: Peanut Butter Squares
steps: Mix all ingredients together except chocolate chips.
Press into a cookie sheet.
Melt chocolate chips and spread over the top.
Refrigerate until firm and cut into squares.
notes: Easiest to cut at room temperature so the chocolate does not crack as much.

title: Tollhouse Pie

ingredients.n: butter, melted and cooled to room temperature
Whipped cream or vanilla ice cream, for serving

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a large bowl, beat eggs until foamy. Beat in flour, sugar, and brown sugar until well blended. Blend in melted butter. Stir in chocolate chips and walnuts. Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 325°F for 1 hour.
Serve warm with whipped cream or ice cream.
notes: Course tagged "Cakes" for now — the taxonomy has no pie category.

title: Nonna's Peanut Butter Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. In a medium bowl, combine dry ingredients and set aside.
In a large bowl, mix butter, peanut butter, white sugar, and brown sugar until well combined. Add eggs and mix well.
Add dry ingredients to the butter and sugar mixture and blend until just combined.
Roll into 1-inch balls, coat with white sugar, then press onto a cookie sheet with a fork in a crisscross pattern.
Bake 10–12 minutes, or until lightly brown on the edges.

title: Jewish Apple Cake
steps: Peel and slice apples. Sprinkle with cinnamon and 5 tablespoons sugar; set aside.
Combine flour, 2 cups sugar, oil, eggs, baking powder, orange juice, vanilla, and almond extract; mix well.
Grease and flour a tube pan. Put half the batter in the pan and cover with half the apple mixture. Add remaining batter and top with remaining apples. Sprinkle with chopped walnuts if desired.
Bake at 350°F for about 1 3/4 hours, or until done.
notes: Two separate sugar measurements — one for the apples, one for the batter. Marked in the ingredient names.

title: Oreo Bonbons
steps: Coarsely chop 12 cookies and set aside. Process the remaining cookies into fine crumbs and set aside.
Beat cream cheese, dry milk, and vanilla with an electric mixer at medium speed until smooth.
Beat in powdered sugar, 1 cup at a time, at low speed until mixture is smooth.
Stir in reserved chopped cookies. Refrigerate 2 hours or until firm.
Use a small cookie scoop to form balls, then roll in cookie crumbs. Store in the refrigerator.

title: Jesse's Almond Cookies

ingredients.n: powdered sugar, optional, for rolling or dusting

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form.
Gently stir almond extract into the whipped egg whites.
Combine almond flour and granulated sugar in a separate medium bowl.
Fold the almond-flour mixture into the whipped egg whites with a spatula until a thick, cohesive dough forms.
Scoop tablespoon-size portions, roll into balls, and coat in powdered sugar if desired.
Bake 18–22 minutes, until edges turn lightly golden.
notes: Very close to Italian Amaretti Cookies (collected) — same four core ingredients, different ratios and a lower oven. Kept separate deliberately.

title: Restaurant-Style Salsa
source: The Pioneer Woman — Restaurant-Style Salsa

ingredients.n: diced tomatoes with green chilies, such as Rotel
fresh cilantro, plus more to taste

steps: Add the whole tomatoes and their juice, diced tomatoes with green chilies, onion, jalapeño, garlic, sugar, salt, cumin, lime juice, and cilantro to a food processor.
Pulse until the salsa reaches your preferred consistency; about 10–15 pulses gives a smooth restaurant-style texture.
Taste with a tortilla chip and adjust seasoning, cilantro, or lime juice as desired.
Transfer to a covered container and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
Serve chilled with tortilla chips or alongside Mexican dishes.
notes: For milder salsa, remove the jalapeño seeds and membrane. For more heat, leave them in or add more jalapeño.
The salsa tends to get spicier as it sits.
Keeps refrigerated in a covered container up to 7 days.

title: Best Classic Shepherd's Pie
source: The Wholesome Dish — The Best Classic Shepherd's Pie

ingredients.n: 90% lean ground beef or ground lamb
russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes (topping)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook about 5 minutes.
Add the beef or lamb and season with parsley, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper. Cook 6–8 minutes, breaking up the meat as it browns.
Stir in the Worcestershire sauce and garlic; cook 1 minute.
Add the flour and tomato paste and stir until fully incorporated.
Add the beef broth, peas and carrots, and corn. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
Boil the potatoes 10–15 minutes until fork-tender. Drain and return to the hot pot for 1 minute to dry.
Add the butter, half-and-half, garlic powder, salt, and pepper and mash smooth. Stir in the Parmesan.
Spread the meat mixture in a 9x9-inch or 7x11-inch baking dish and top evenly with the mashed potatoes.
Bake uncovered 25–30 minutes. Rest 15 minutes before serving.
notes: Ground lamb makes traditional Shepherd's Pie; ground beef makes Cottage Pie.
Can be assembled ahead and refrigerated up to 3 days before baking.

title: Easy Breakfast Casserole
source: All Things Mamma — Easy Breakfast Casserole
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Brown and crumble the sausage in a skillet.
Whisk the eggs and milk together, then stir in the salt and pepper.
Coat a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Add the hash browns, sausage, and cheese to the dish and stir together.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the top.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake 10–15 minutes more, until the center is set.
notes: Can be assembled the night before and refrigerated; allow extra baking time if going in cold.
Bacon, ham, turkey sausage, vegetables, or other melting cheeses all substitute well.

title: Granola Bar Bites
source: Real Life Dinner — Granola Bar Bites
steps: Combine the cereal, oats, nuts, raisins, flaxseed, chia seeds, coconut oil, and vanilla in a large bowl.
Microwave the honey and agave for 1 minute 30 seconds.
Stir the marshmallows into the hot mixture until melted, microwaving another 10–15 seconds if needed.
Stir in the peanut butter until smooth.
Pour over the dry ingredients and stir until everything is coated.
Cool 2–3 minutes, then gently mix in the mini M&M's.
Portion with a cookie scoop and form into balls.
Refrigerate or freeze a couple of hours before serving.
notes: A plastic bag over your hand helps when shaping the sticky mixture.
The coconut oil, chia, and flaxseed are all optional.
Keep refrigerated or frozen.

title: Creamy Cilantro Verde Enchiladas
source: Real Life Dinner — Creamy Cilantro Verde Enchiladas

ingredients.n: cooked chicken breast, cubed or shredded
small white or yellow onion, chopped

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Blend the salsa verde, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, and salt.
Add the cream cheese and blend until smooth.
Mix the cooked chicken with about two-thirds of the sauce.
Spread a little of the remaining sauce in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Fill each tortilla with about 1/2 cup of the chicken mixture, roll, and arrange in the dish.
Spread the remaining sauce over the enchiladas.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes.
Uncover, top with the Monterey Jack, and bake 10–15 minutes more.
notes: Rotisserie chicken works well here.
Use full-fat cream cheese for the intended texture.
Can be assembled ahead and frozen.

title: Savannah Strawberry Tall Cake
source: Paula Deen — Savannah Strawberry Tall Cake

ingredients.n: white cake mix, prepared and baked in three 8-inch round pans
granulated sugar, divided (1/3 cup for the berries, 1 cup for the cream)

steps: Combine the strawberries with 1/3 cup of the sugar and refrigerate.
Prepare the cake mix and bake in three 8-inch round pans until done, about 15–20 minutes. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, remaining 1 cup sugar, and vanilla until light and fluffy.
With the mixer on low, slowly add the heavy cream, then increase speed and whip to stiff peaks.
Layer cake, strawberries, and the whipped cream mixture, repeating for all three layers.
Decorate the top with the remaining strawberries and serve with extra cream mixture alongside.
notes: Cool the cake layers completely before assembly.
Macerating the strawberries creates a sweet syrup.
The cream cheese should be at room temperature.

title: Bread Machine Cinnamon Rolls
source: Thriving Home — Bread Machine Cinnamon Rolls

ingredients.n: butter, softened and cut into chunks

steps: Add the dough ingredients to the bread machine in the order listed and run the dough cycle.
Combine the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Divide the finished dough in half. Roll one half into about an 18x12-inch rectangle.
Brush with half the melted butter and sprinkle with half the cinnamon sugar.
Roll up from a long edge into a log and slice into about 1-inch rolls.
Repeat with the remaining dough. Arrange on a greased baking sheet.
Cover and rise 25–30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°F and bake 17–20 minutes.
Whisk the powdered sugar, vanilla, and milk and drizzle over the warm rolls.
notes: A metal baking sheet helps caramelize the bottoms.
For a stand mixer instead, knead 7–8 minutes and let rise 1–1 1/2 hours.
Unbaked rolls can be frozen up to 3 months.

title: The Best Instant Pot Macaroni and Cheese
source: Real Life Dinner — The Best Instant Pot Macaroni and Cheese
steps: Add the pasta, hot sauce, seasonings, butter, and broth to a 6- or 8-quart Instant Pot.
Stir and gently press the pasta down into the broth.
Cook on High Pressure for 5 minutes.
Quick-release the pressure carefully.
Stir in the milk first, then the cheeses, until smooth and melted.
Add a little more milk if needed and serve immediately.
notes: Medium shells are especially good at holding the sauce.
Freshly shredded cheese melts most smoothly.
Leftovers keep refrigerated up to 5 days.

title: Easy One-Hour Dinner Rolls
source: Cooking Classy — Easy One-Hour Dinner Rolls

ingredients.n: unsalted butter, cut into pieces, plus more for the tops

steps: Preheat oven to 180°F.
Whisk 3 1/2 cups of the flour, the sugar, yeast, and salt in a stand mixer bowl.
Heat the water, milk, and butter to about 120°F.
Add the warm liquid and lemon juice to the dry ingredients.
Knead with the dough hook about 3 minutes, adding flour only as needed.
Cover and rest 5 minutes. Butter a 9x13-inch dish.
Divide the dough into 15 rolls and arrange in the dish.
Place in the 180°F oven, turn the oven off immediately, and rise 20 minutes without opening the door.
Remove the rolls and preheat the oven to 375°F.
Bake 14–16 minutes until golden. Butter the tops immediately.
notes: Rapid-rise yeast is what makes the one-hour timeline work.
Do not overheat the milk mixture or over-knead the dough.
Baked rolls freeze up to 3 months.

title: Chef John's Italian Meatballs
source: Allrecipes — Chef John's Italian Meatballs
steps: Line a baking sheet with foil and grease it lightly.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk or broth for 20 minutes.
Cook the onion in the olive oil 5 minutes over medium heat, then about 15 minutes over low heat until tender.
Gently combine the beef, pork, onion, soaked breadcrumbs, eggs, Parmesan, parsley, garlic, and seasonings.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 425°F.
Form 1 1/2-inch meatballs and arrange on the baking sheet.
Bake 15–20 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Serve with tomato sauce, or simmer in the sauce 1–2 hours.
notes: An 80/20 ground beef blend keeps the meatballs juicy.
Avoid overmixing.
Cooked meatballs freeze well up to 3 months.

title: Homemade Pasta
source: Love & Lemons — Homemade Pasta
steps: Mound the flour on a clean surface and make a well in the center.
Add the eggs, olive oil, and salt, gradually incorporating the flour with a fork.
Bring the dough together and knead 8–10 minutes until smooth.
Wrap tightly and rest at room temperature 30 minutes.
Divide into 4 pieces and roll progressively thinner through a pasta roller.
Cut into the shape you want, such as fettuccine.
Boil in well-salted water 1–2 minutes.
Drain and serve immediately.
notes: All-purpose flour works well; 00 flour is not required.
If the dough is dry, lightly wet your fingers while kneading; if sticky, dust with flour.
Fresh pasta cooks very quickly — watch it closely.

title: Japchae (Korean Noodles)
source: RecipeTin Eats — Japchae

ingredients.n: boneless beef short ribs or ribeye, thinly sliced

steps: Marinate the sliced beef with the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and pepper for 15–20 minutes.
Combine the noodle dressing ingredients in a very large bowl.
Cook the sweet potato noodles per package directions; drain, rinse briefly, and add to the dressing bowl.
Stir-fry the onion, green onion whites, and mushrooms; transfer to the bowl.
Stir-fry the carrots and bell pepper, then add the spinach and green onion greens; transfer to the bowl.
Stir-fry the marinated beef until just cooked; transfer to the bowl.
Add the sesame seeds and toss everything thoroughly.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Dangmyeon are Korean sweet potato starch noodles.
Use light or all-purpose soy sauce, not dark soy sauce.
Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days.

title: Fried Scones (Utah Scones)
source: Creme de la Crumb — Fried Scones

ingredients.n: Honey, powdered sugar, butter, or syrup, for serving

steps: Combine the yeast with 3 Tbsp warm water and a pinch of sugar; let stand 10 minutes until foamy.
Combine the hot water, oil, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Stir the beaten egg into the yeast mixture, then add to the oil mixture.
Gradually add the flour and knead about 5 minutes until elastic and smooth.
Place in a greased bowl and rise about 30 minutes, until doubled.
Heat 2 inches of frying oil to 350–375°F.
Punch down the dough and divide into 12 balls. Roll or stretch each to about 1/4 inch thick.
Fry 2–3 at a time, 1–2 minutes per side, until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
notes: Honey and powdered sugar is the classic topping.
Keep the oil between 350–375°F.
Prepared dough can be refrigerated up to 3 days.

title: Cilantro Jalapeño Sauce
source: Fifteen Spatulas — Cilantro Jalapeno Sauce
steps: Remove the jalapeño seeds and ribs for a milder sauce, or leave them in for more heat.
Roughly chop the jalapeños.
Blend the jalapeños, cilantro, garlic, mayonnaise, lime juice, oil, salt, and pepper on high for at least 30 seconds, until smooth.
Taste and adjust the seasoning or lime.
For the best flavor, refrigerate a few hours before serving.
notes: Cilantro stems can go in too.
Olive oil can replace the avocado oil.
Refrigerate airtight up to 1 week; freezing is not recommended.

title: Easy Teriyaki Chicken Marinade
source: Real Food Whole Life — Teriyaki Chicken Marinade

ingredients.n: boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and garlic until the sugar dissolves. Reserve half for serving.

To grill: marinate the chicken in the remaining half plus 2 Tbsp water for 30–60 minutes. Grill over medium-high heat until thighs reach 170°F or breasts reach 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, slice, and drizzle with the reserved marinade.

To bake: preheat oven to 425°F. Bake the chicken with half the marinade 20–25 minutes, to a safe temperature. Broil 2–3 minutes for caramelization if you like. Rest, slice, and drizzle with the reserved marinade.
notes: Use reduced-sodium soy sauce — regular makes this too salty.
Mirin can replace the rice vinegar.
Raw marinated chicken can be frozen up to 3 months.

title: The Best Fudgy Brownies
source: Inspired Taste — The Best Fudgy Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F. Line an 8x8-inch pan with parchment or foil.
Melt the butter over medium-low heat and remove from heat before it browns.
Stir in the sugar, cocoa, vanilla, and salt. Cool 5–10 minutes.
Add the eggs one at a time, stirring vigorously after each.
Add the flour and beat 40–50 strokes, until thick and glossy.
Fold in the nuts or chips if using.
Spread in the pan and bake 20–30 minutes; the center should still look slightly underdone.
Cool completely before slicing.
notes: Do not overbake — this is the whole trick to the fudgy texture.
A metal pan is recommended.
Freezes up to 3 months.

title: Delicious Ham and Potato Soup
source: Allrecipes — Delicious Ham and Potato Soup
steps: Combine the potatoes, water, ham, celery, and onion in a stockpot.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer 10–15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the bouillon, pepper, and salt.
In a separate saucepan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook 4–5 minutes until smooth and thick.
Pour the milk mixture into the soup, stir, and heat through.
Taste and adjust the seasoning.
notes: A good landing spot for leftover holiday ham.
Optional toppings: cheddar, bacon, green onions, or chives.
Refrigerate up to 4 days; freezing is not recommended.

title: Chicken Piccata
source: Spend With Pennies — Chicken Piccata

ingredients.n: olive oil, plus more as needed
dry white wine or extra broth

steps: Pound the chicken to about 1/2 inch thick.
Combine the flour, lemon zest, salt, and pepper and dredge the chicken.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 4–5 minutes per side, to 165°F. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Melt the butter and whisk in the 1 1/2 Tbsp flour. Cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the broth. Add the lemon juice, wine, and capers and simmer 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and simmer 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and serve.
notes: Fresh lemon juice makes a real difference here.
The wine can be replaced with more chicken broth.
Refrigerate leftovers up to 4 days.

title: KitchenAid Crusty Pizza Dough (Triple Batch)
source: Food.com — KitchenAid Crusty Pizza Dough

ingredients.n: all-purpose flour, added gradually as needed

steps: Add the warm water to a warmed KitchenAid bowl and dissolve the yeast.
Add the salt, olive oil, and about 7 1/2 cups of the flour.
Mix with the dough hook on Speed 2 for 1 minute.
Continue on Speed 2, adding flour about 1/2 cup at a time, until the dough clings to the hook and pulls away from the sides.
Knead on Speed 2 for 2 minutes.
Place in a greased bowl, cover, and rise about 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down and divide into 3 equal portions.
Brush three 14-inch pizza pans with olive oil and stretch the dough onto the pans.
Add toppings and bake at 450°F for 15–20 minutes.
notes: This is already the 3x-scaled version of the original recipe — the single batch makes one 14-inch pizza.
The yeast amount, 3/4 oz, is three standard 1/4 oz packets (about 6 3/4 tsp).
Do not automatically use all the flour; add only what the dough needs.
Keep the KitchenAid at Speed 2 while kneading with the dough hook.

title: Turkey and Stuffing Meatballs
source: The Cozy Cook — Turkey and Stuffing Meatballs

ingredients.n: turkey or chicken Stove Top stuffing

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Melt 2 Tbsp of the butter and cook the onion and celery 5–6 minutes.
Add the remaining butter, the broth, and the water and bring to a boil.
Add the stuffing mix, reduce heat, stir, then remove from heat. Cool 2–3 minutes.
Add the seasoned ground turkey, sausage, and egg and mix evenly.
Form about 1 3/4-inch meatballs and arrange on a lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake 15 minutes.
Broil at 450°F for up to 2 minutes to brown the tops.
notes: Chop the vegetables finely so the meatballs hold together.
Ground chicken can replace the turkey.
Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: The Best Leftover Turkey Soup
source: Mel's Kitchen Cafe — The Best Leftover Turkey Soup

ingredients.n: brown rice or brown rice blend

steps: Heat the butter and oil in a 6-quart pot.
Add the carrots, celery, onion, thyme, and rosemary and cook 3–4 minutes.
Add the broth, rice, salt, and pepper. Simmer until the rice is tender, about 30 minutes for a brown or wild blend.
Blend or whisk the half-and-half with the flour until smooth.
Slowly whisk the mixture into the soup and simmer 5–6 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Stir in the turkey and heat through.
Adjust the seasoning and serve.
notes: Chicken works just as well as turkey.
1% or 2% milk can replace the half-and-half, though the soup will be less rich.
Homemade turkey stock is excellent here.

title: Shrimp Scampi with Zoodles
source: Feel Good Foodie — Shrimp Scampi with Zoodles
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and crushed red pepper and cook about 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and season with the paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook 3–4 minutes until pink and opaque, then remove the shrimp.
Add the broth, lemon juice, and red wine vinegar, scrape up the browned bits, and bring to a boil.
Turn off the heat and return the shrimp along with the zucchini noodles.
Toss just until the zoodles are warmed and coated. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not overcook the shrimp — they finish in the residual heat.
Thaw and pat frozen shrimp dry before cooking.
Best eaten the same day; freezing is not recommended.

title: Easy Homemade Beef Stew
source: Healthy Fitness Meals — Easy Homemade Beef Stew

ingredients.n: beef chuck roast, cut into chunks
Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into chunks

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Season the beef with the salt and pepper, then toss with the flour.
Brown the beef in the oil in batches, 3–4 minutes per batch. Set aside.
Cook the onion, garlic, and carrots 2–3 minutes.
Add the potatoes, broth, tomato paste, bay leaf, thyme, and Worcestershire, scraping up the browned bits.
Bring to a simmer and return the beef to the pot.
Cover and bake 2–2 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender.
Discard the bay leaf and adjust the seasoning.
notes: Brown the beef in batches or it steams instead of searing.
For a thicker stew, simmer uncovered at the end or use a cornstarch slurry.
Slow cooker and pressure cooker methods also work.

title: Fluffy, Bubbly & Chewy Naan
source: RecipeTin Eats — Naan
steps: Combine the yeast, warm water, and sugar and let stand 10 minutes until foamy.
Whisk the milk and egg together separately.
Sift the flour and salt, make a well, and add the yeast mixture, melted ghee, and milk-egg mixture.
Mix into a soft, slightly sticky dough. No kneading required.
Cover and rise 1–1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Divide into 6 balls and rise another 15 minutes.
Roll each to about 1/8 inch thick and 6–7 inches wide.
Heat a lightly oiled cast-iron skillet over high heat.
Cook each naan 60–90 seconds on the first side, then 45–60 seconds on the second.
Brush immediately with melted ghee or butter.
notes: Bread flour gives especially fluffy naan, but all-purpose works.
High heat matters — each naan should cook in about 2–2 1/2 minutes total.
For garlic butter, mix the crushed garlic into the melted ghee or butter.

title: Rustic No-Knead Bread
source: Pampered Chef — Rustic No-Knead Bread
steps: Combine 3 1/2 cups of the flour with the sugar, yeast, and salt.
Add the warm water and 2 Tbsp of the olive oil. Beat on low until moistened, then on medium for 3 minutes.
Add the remaining flour and mix into a stiff, slightly sticky dough.
Cover and rise in a warm place about 1 hour, until doubled.
Stir the dough down to deflate it.
Brush a Dutch oven with the remaining oil, scrape in the dough, and shape into a mound. Turn once to coat the top.
Sprinkle with the optional topping and rise uncovered 25–30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°F.
Bake uncovered 40–45 minutes, until deep golden.
Cool at least 30 minutes before removing and slicing.
notes: Bread flour is recommended over all-purpose.
Quick-rise yeast can shorten the rise time.
No hand-kneading required at any point.

title: Homemade Teriyaki Sauce
source: The Modern Proper — Homemade Teriyaki Sauce
steps: Whisk the cornstarch and cold water until smooth.
Whisk in the brown sugar, soy sauce, honey, ginger, and garlic powder.
Pour into a small saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Reduce to medium and cook about 5 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Remove from heat; the sauce keeps thickening as it cools.
notes: Use tamari instead of soy sauce for a gluten-free version.
Good on chicken, stir-fries, vegetables, rice bowls, and as a marinade.
Refrigerate airtight up to 1 week.

title: Queso Dip (Mexican Cheese Dip)
source: RecipeTin Eats — Queso Dip
steps: Toss the shredded cheese with the cornstarch.
Melt the butter over medium heat and cook the garlic and onion about 3 minutes, until translucent.
Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes.
Add the evaporated milk and cheese, then the green chiles and seasonings.
Stir until smooth and silky.
Season with salt and stir in the cilantro.
Thin with 2–3 Tbsp milk or water as needed and serve warm.
notes: Shred the cheese yourself — pre-shredded has anti-caking agents that turn the dip grainy.
Pepper Jack can replace part of the cheddar for more heat.
Refrigerate up to 5 days; reheat with a splash of milk.

title: Homemade Miso Soup with Tofu
source: Just One Cookbook — Homemade Miso Soup
steps: Slice the green onion.
For the dashi, add the water and kombu to a saucepan and soak 30 minutes if you have time.
Heat slowly over medium-low about 10 minutes, removing the kombu just before it boils.
Add the katsuobushi, bring back to a boil, simmer 30 seconds, turn off the heat, and let stand 10 minutes.
Strain the dashi and return it to the saucepan.
Warm the dashi, then turn off the heat before adding the miso.
Dissolve the miso in a ladle or small bowl with some hot dashi, then stir it back into the soup.
Add the cubed tofu, wakame, and green onion. Serve warm, without boiling.
notes: A good starting ratio is 1 Tbsp miso per cup of dashi.
Do not boil the soup after adding the miso — it dulls the flavor.
The katsuobushi is dried fish, so this is not vegetarian as written. For a vegetarian version, use kombu or kombu-shiitake dashi.

title: Authentic Watergate Salad
source: Food.com — Authentic Watergate Salad
steps: Combine the dry pudding mix, undrained pineapple, marshmallows, and nuts.
Stir thoroughly.
Gently fold in the whipped topping until evenly incorporated.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
notes: Do not prepare the pudding separately — the dry mix goes straight in.
Do not drain the pineapple; the juice sets the pudding.
Pecans are the popular nut choice.

title: Grandma's Irish Soda Bread
source: Sally's Baking — Grandma's Irish Soda Bread

ingredients.n: unsalted butter, very cold and cubed

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Prepare a cast-iron skillet, cake pan, pie pan, Dutch oven, or lined baking sheet.
Whisk the buttermilk and egg together.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt.
Cut the cold butter into the flour mixture until pea-sized crumbs form.
Stir in the raisins if using.
Add the buttermilk mixture and fold until the dough is too stiff to stir.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and gently knead about 30 seconds, just to bring it together.
Shape into a ball, transfer to the pan, and cut a 1/2-inch-deep X on top.
Bake 45–55 minutes, tenting with foil if it browns too fast. The center should reach about 195°F.
Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then transfer to a rack.
notes: Cold butter and minimal handling are what keep the texture tender.
Buttermilk is not optional — the acid is what activates the baking soda.
Store covered up to 2 days at room temperature, or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Out of This World Carrot Cake with Callie's Cream Cheese Frosting
source: Real Life Dinner — Out of This World Carrot Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour two 9-inch round pans and line the bottoms with parchment.
To make sour milk, add 1 tsp lemon juice to a measuring cup plus enough milk to equal 3/4 cup; let stand 3–5 minutes.
Mix the sugar, oil, eggs, and sour milk, then add the vanilla.
Add the flour, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt and mix just until incorporated.
Fold in the carrots, undrained pineapple, coconut, walnuts, and raisins if using.
Divide between the pans and bake 45–50 minutes. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar, and vanilla until smooth.
Layer and frost the cake: apply a thin crumb coat, chill about 20 minutes, then finish frosting.
notes: Shred the carrots finely — coarse shreds stay firm in the crumb.
Do not drain the pineapple.
Buttermilk can replace the sour milk.

title: Steak Fajitas
source: Add a Pinch — Steak Fajitas

ingredients.n: skirt, flank, sirloin, or hanger steak, sliced into 1/2-inch strips

steps: Place the steak in one sealable bag and the peppers and onion in another.
Shake the olive oil, lime juice, seasonings, and garlic together.
Pour one-third of the marinade over the steak, one-third over the vegetables, and reserve the final third.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Cook the vegetables in a hot skillet about 5 minutes, then remove.
Cook the steak 7–10 minutes, to your preferred doneness.
Return the vegetables and add the reserved marinade; toss until hot.
Serve with warm tortillas.
notes: Keep the meat and vegetables in separate bags while marinating.
Set aside the reserved third of the marinade before any of it touches raw meat.
Sour cream, guacamole, and salsa are all good on top.

title: Tres Leches Cake
source: Tastes Better From Scratch — Tres Leches Cake

ingredients.n: granulated sugar, divided (3/4 cup for the yolks, 1/4 cup for the whites)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the egg yolks with 3/4 cup of the sugar until pale, then stir in the 1/3 cup milk and vanilla.
Gently combine the yolk mixture with the flour mixture.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, gradually adding the remaining 1/4 cup sugar.
Fold the whites into the batter and pour into an ungreased 9x13-inch pan.
Bake 25–35 minutes and cool completely.
Combine the evaporated milk, condensed milk, and 1/4 cup whole milk.
Poke the cooled cake all over with a fork and slowly pour the milk mixture over it.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla to stiff peaks and spread over the cake.
Dust with cinnamon and add strawberries if you like.
notes: Do not grease the pan — the batter needs to climb the sides.
This is excellent made the night before.
Keep refrigerated.

title: Easy Instant Pot Refried Beans
source: Five Heart Home — Instant Pot Refried Beans

ingredients.n: dried pinto beans, rinsed and sorted

steps: Use Sauté mode to heat the oil, then cook the onion, garlic, and jalapeño 2 minutes. Cancel Sauté.
Add the beans, green chiles, broth, vinegar, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Cook on High Pressure for 50 minutes.
Natural-release 20 minutes, then vent the remaining pressure.
Reserve the cooking liquid and drain the beans.
Return the beans to the pot and purée with an immersion blender.
Add 1/2–1 cup of the reserved liquid gradually, to your preferred consistency.
Adjust the seasoning and serve.
notes: No soaking required.
Use vegetable broth to make this vegan.
Refrigerate up to 1 week or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Chicken Parmesan
source: Ask Chef Dennis — Chicken Parmesan

ingredients.n: boneless skinless chicken breasts, about 6 oz each

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Pound the chicken to an even thickness.
Set up seasoned flour, egg wash, and breadcrumbs in three shallow dishes.
Coat the chicken in flour, then egg wash, then breadcrumbs.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil to around 350°F.
Fry the chicken 2–3 minutes per side until golden, then drain on a wire rack.
Arrange in a baking dish, top each piece with marinara and mozzarella, and sprinkle with parsley.
Bake about 20 minutes, until the cheese melts and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Serve immediately.
notes: Do not overcrowd the skillet.
Keeping the oil hot is what prevents greasy breading.
Fresh mozzarella can replace the shredded.

title: The Best Blondies
source: Sugar Spun Run — The Best Blondies
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 9x13-inch metal pan with parchment.
Stir the melted butter with the brown and granulated sugars.
Add the eggs, yolk, and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt separately.
Gradually stir the dry ingredients into the wet, just until combined.
Fold in the white chocolate chips and walnuts if using.
Spread in the pan and bake 25–30 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden and the center has fudgy crumbs.
Cool completely before slicing.
notes: Do not overbake.
Up to 2 cups of add-ins total works fine.
Store airtight at room temperature up to 4 days.

title: Cilantro Lime Rice
source: Fifteen Spatulas — Cilantro Lime Rice
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water about 2 minutes, until the water runs clear, then drain 2 minutes.
Heat the ghee, butter, or oil in a large nonstick pan with a tight-fitting lid.
Toast the rice 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the water and salt, cover, and bring to a boil.
Reduce to medium-low and cook covered 20 minutes without lifting the lid or stirring.
Remove from heat, fluff, and rest uncovered 5 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro, lime juice, and lime zest.
notes: Basmati is especially good here, though jasmine works.
Rinsing and toasting are what keep the grains separate.
Refrigerate airtight up to 5 days.

title: Copycat Chipotle Chicken
source: Brown Eyed Baker — Copycat Chipotle Chicken
steps: Blend the onion, garlic, adobo, olive oil, ancho chile powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Add water as needed to bring the marinade to 1 cup.
Poke the chicken with a fork, place in a resealable bag, add the marinade, and coat well.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Heat a lightly oiled cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through to at least 165°F.
Rest at least 10 minutes, then chop or slice.
notes: Thighs stay noticeably juicier than breasts here.
For more heat, add some of the actual chipotle peppers, not just the adobo sauce.
Cooked chicken refrigerates up to 4 days.

title: Chipotle Corn Salsa (Copycat)
source: Culinary Hill — Chipotle Corn Salsa

ingredients.n: jalapeño peppers, seeded and finely chopped

steps: Roast the poblano over a gas flame until charred on all sides, about 2–3 minutes.
Place in a covered bowl and steam 10 minutes.
Rub off the charred skin, remove the stem and seeds, and finely chop.
Cook the frozen corn according to package directions and cool completely.
Combine the corn, poblano, red onion, jalapeños, and cilantro.
Add the lemon and lime juices, toss, and season with salt.
Serve immediately or chill a few hours.
notes: Remove the jalapeño seeds and membranes for a milder salsa.
Fresh corn can replace the frozen.
Refrigerate airtight up to 4 days.

title: Cherry Pie Bars
source: Bunsen Burner Bakery — Cherry Pie Bars

ingredients.n: fresh or frozen cherries, pitted and halved

steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a 9x9-inch pan with foil and grease lightly.
Pulse the flour, powdered sugar, and salt in a food processor. Add the butter and pulse to a coarse-sand texture.
Reserve about 3/4 cup of the mixture for topping and press the rest into the pan.
Bake the crust 12 minutes.
Combine the cherries, cornstarch, lemon juice, and granulated sugar.
Spread the cherry mixture over the crust and crumble the reserved shortbread mixture on top.
Bake 25–30 minutes, until the filling bubbles and the topping is golden.
Cool completely in the pan, at least 1 hour, before slicing.
notes: If using frozen cherries, thaw and drain the excess liquid first.
The full hour of cooling is what lets the filling set.
Freezes up to 3 months.
